name: K-feldspar

matrix.title: Flattening on (010) × elongation axis
matrix.subtitle: Rows flatten the crystal on b{010}, from adularia-like crystals to thin sanidine tablets. Columns move the elongation from [100] (square c–b section, the shape of Baveno-twinned crystals) through equant to [001] (the Carlsbad-type prism).
matrix.note: Eight interfacial angles match Dana (1892) to within 0.2°, for example c∧x = 50.21° against 50°16.5′. Sanidine, orthoclase and adularia cells differ by less than 0.5%. Microcline (C1̄) has the same forms and habits. Carlsbad, Baveno and Manebach are twin laws, not single convex crystals, so they are not modelled. The Handbook of Mineralogy's orthoclase c = 7.299 Å is a typo for 7.2099 Å.

about: K-feldspar is built from a handful of forms: the pinacoids b{010} and c{001}, the prism m{110} and the pinacoids x{1̄01} and y{2̄01}. Changing their relative sizes moves the crystal between tablets flattened on (010) (sanidine), prisms along c, crystals elongated along a, and the pseudo-orthorhombic adularia of Alpine veins. Megacrysts in granites are phenocrysts with inclusion zoning (Vernon 1986), and their size distributions record thermal history (Higgins 1999). In thermochronology, K-feldspar's internal diffusion domains are modelled with the MDD approach (Lovera et al. 1989).

habits.name: Prismatic ∥ c
habits.text: b + m prism with c, x, y ends: common orthoclase and the habit of Carlsbad twins (column [001]+).

habits.name: Elongated ∥ a
habits.text: A square c–b prism, as in Baveno-twinned crystals (column [100]+).

habits.name: Adularia
habits.text: m + x + c with little b: pseudo-orthorhombic or rhombohedral-looking (row B0).

habits.name: Sanidine tablets
habits.text: Tabular on (010), typical of volcanic sanidine (rows B3–B4).

references.citation: Prince, E., Donnay, G., Martin, R.F. (1973). Neutron diffraction refinement of an ordered orthoclase structure. American Mineralogist 58, 500–507.
Vernon, R.H. (1986). K-feldspar megacrysts in granites — phenocrysts, not porphyroblasts. Earth-Science Reviews 23, 1–63.
references.note: Origin, habit and inclusion zoning of megacrysts.

references.citation: Higgins, M.D. (1999). Origin of megacrysts in granitoids by textural coarsening: a crystal size distribution (CSD) study of microcline in the Cathedral Peak Granodiorite. Geological Society, London, Special Publications 168, 207–219.
references.note: K-feldspar crystal size distributions and thermal history.

references.citation: Lovera, O.M., Richter, F.M., Harrison, T.M. (1989). The 40Ar/39Ar thermochronometry for slowly cooled samples having a distribution of diffusion domain sizes. Journal of Geophysical Research 94, 17917–17935.
Smith, J.V., Brown, W.L. (1988). Feldspar Minerals, Vol. 1, 2nd ed. Springer.
references.note: The standard reference for feldspar crystallography and morphology.

references.citation: Higgins, M.D. (1994). Numerical modeling of crystal shapes in thin sections: estimation of crystal habit and true size. American Mineralogist 79, 113–119.
Morgan, D.J., Jerram, D.A. (2006). On estimating crystal shape for crystal size distribution analysis. Journal of Volcanology and Geothermal Research 154, 1–7.
references.note: Estimating short:intermediate:long shape for crystal size distributions.
